question: does the mask flip because cells sit on the threshold (dither) or because the subject moved?
granularity: dot (2x4 pixel block per cell, one byte per cell)
control_comparison: the tone control is per CELL and is compared against the mask's per-CELL change rate; the previous run compared it against the mask's ON-THRESHOLD per-dot rate, which is the most volatile bin and not a like-for-like comparison
verdict: BOTH, and that is the actual finding. Flip rate falls monotonically from 19.18% on the threshold to 0.36% far from it (52.6x), so a large part of the raw delta is threshold dither. But the far-from-threshold floor of 0.36% is BELOW the 39.98% independence baseline, so that residual is structured, not noise -- there is genuine change to build on. The tone control came back at 5.41% per cell against 9.67% per cell for the mask, so the argmax ramp is BETTER than the mask, and the fallback is supported by its own control.
consequence: Two things follow, and the second is the one that matters. First, the fix for the noisy half is hysteresis: keep a dot's bit until its luma crosses the threshold by a margin, not a single bare comparison. The measured gradient sizes it: a dot ON the threshold flips 19.18% of the time, a dot 11-20 counts away flips 1.76%, and a dot 41+ counts away flips 0.36% -- so a margin of a couple of dozen counts separates the two populations by more than an order of magnitude. Second, the tone channel is now measured against the mask on the same frames and on the same basis (per cell), and it is the more stable of the two -- so the tone channel, not the mask, is the one to build motion on.

renderer.note: the character renderer assumes the STANDARD NV12 stride of 23,040 bytes per frame, so the capture is re-wrapped into standard NV12 first; no luma byte is changed by that re-wrap

supersedes.why: Re-measured on 2026-10-20. The previous run read the capture at W*H*3//2 = 23,040 bytes per frame; the capture on disk carries 19,200 bytes per frame, so all but every sixth frame was torn (rows 0..71 from frame k, rows 72..95 from frame k+1). The previous numbers are recorded here rather than silently overwritten.
supersedes.previous_tone_comparison_basis: the previous run compared the tone's per-cell rate (70.91%) against the mask's ON-THRESHOLD per-dot rate (67.25%) and called the tone WORSE. The mask's overall per-cell rate was not computed, so the comparison was not like for like.
supersedes.previous_verdict: BOTH, and that is the actual finding. Flip rate falls monotonically from 67.25% on the threshold to 21.61% far from it (3.1x), so roughly half the raw delta is threshold dither. But the far-from-threshold floor of 21.61% is BELOW the 34.62% independence baseline, so that residual is structured, not noise -- there is genuine change to build on. The tone control came back at 70.91%, WORSE than the mask, so the argmax ramp is not a more stable channel and the fallback is refuted by its own control.
supersedes.previous_consequence: Two things follow, and the second is the one that matters. First, the fix for the noisy half is hysteresis: keep a dot's bit until its luma crosses the threshold by a margin, not a single bare comparison. The measured gradient sizes it -- a dot more than ~20 counts from the threshold is already 1.6x more stable than one on it, so a margin of that order separates the two populations. Second, the tone channel must NOT be the fallback: at 70.91% it flips more than the mask and carries less stable content. Any P-frame built on tone would be worse, not better.
supersedes.consequence_changed: The hysteresis advice SURVIVES and gets sharper -- the separation between a dot on the threshold and one 41+ counts away is now 53x rather than 3.1x, so a margin of a couple of dozen counts is comfortably enough. The advice about the tone channel REVERSES: the previous run compared the tone against the mask's on-threshold per-dot rate and called it worse. Compared like for like, per cell, the tone is the MORE stable channel (5.41% against 9.67%), so the tone channel is the one to build motion on, not the mask.

known_defects_not_fixed.what: the frame-pair loop starts at f = 0, where frames[-1] is the LAST frame, so one spurious pair (last frame vs first frame) is counted as a consecutive pair
known_defects_not_fixed.where: the flip-rate loop and the tone/mask control loop
known_defects_not_fixed.why_not_fixed: it is not the stride defect, and changing it here would confound the old-vs-new comparison that this file exists to make. It is reported instead.
known_defects_not_fixed.effect: one extra pair in nf pairs; it inflates the far-from-threshold floor slightly
